stops.stop: Barahnakar, the coast of the dog-mouthed men
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, and contested as to place: the Rihla gives no date here, and the stop is dated with the Bengal and Sumatra legs that bracket it, fifteen days' sail out of Sonargaon by the book's own count and twenty-five days short of Sumatra. Gibb (1929, p. 366 n. 1) follows Yule in rejecting the older Andaman and Nicobar identifications for the Arakan mainland near the island of Negrais; Beckingham (Hakluyt Society IV, 1994, p. 874 n. 1) calls the people not satisfactorily identified, notes that elephants and a resident Muslim quarter rule out both island groups, and puts the landfall somewhere near Cape Negrais. The pin is Cape Negrais, not an attested landing. Gibb and Beckingham both read Barahnakar as the name of a people rather than of a country
